strengths: Substantial dataset contribution: LEMON is significantly larger (938 hours, 4194 videos, 35 procedures) than existing surgical datasets, addressing a critical bottleneck in surgical computer vision research

Rigorous data curation pipeline: Multi-stage systematic approach with validated classifiers (94.75% F1 storyboard, 95.64% frame classification) for filtering non-surgical content and manual verification

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Tested across 4 downstream tasks and 6 datasets with both linear probing and full fine-tuning protocols, demonstrating consistent improvements (+8.4-9.5pp Jaccard for phase recognition, +8.3pp mDice for segmentation)
Data efficiency demonstrated: LemonFM maintains advantages when fine-tuned on only 50% of labeled data, showing strong generalization capability

Thoughtful surgical-specific augmented distillation: Incorporates k-NN neighbors from same procedure type and temporal neighbors to learn invariance to minor motion and appearance changes, outperforming vanilla DINO

Clear presentation and reproducibility: Excellent figures (especially Fig. 2), comprehensive tables, detailed supplementary material with full hyperparameters, and commitment to public release of dataset, models, and code
Proper ablation studies: Demonstrates importance of dataset curation (+4.5pp F1), effectiveness of augmented distillation (+3.2pp mDice), and architectural choices (ConvNeXt vs ViT)
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: Foundation model essentially applies DINO with surgery-specific augmentations; the main contribution is the dataset rather than technical innovation

Insufficient dataset analysis: Missing statistical analysis of procedure distribution balance, inter-annotator agreement metrics, geographic/equipment bias assessment, and impact of 6% non-standard resolution videos

Generalization claims not fully supported: All downstream test sets are small (e.g., 32 videos for Cholec80, 14 for M2CAI16), and evaluation datasets show procedural overlap; no true out-of-distribution evaluation across different surgical sites, equipment, or countries

YouTube-sourced data limitations not discussed: Potential systematic biases in content, equipment types, and procedural difficulty; video availability risk due to YouTube's terms of service and potential takedowns

Arbitrary technical choices lack justification: k=20 neighbors and 3× distance threshold in augmented distillation have no ablation or principled justification; 1 fps frame extraction may miss rapid surgical motions
New downstream tasks show modest performance: Procedure type classification achieves only 57.8% mAP (authors acknowledge this highlights challenges); limited analysis of task difficulty

Incomplete comparisons and ablations: Augmented distillation only compared against vanilla DINO (not other recent SSL methods); no ablation on video trimming strategy; ConvNeXt-L superiority over ViT-L (+10.7pp mDice) explained only empirically

Data availability and licensing concerns: YouTube video stability not guaranteed, reliance on YouTube Terms of Service creates legal risks, and opt-out mechanism implementation details vague; patient privacy in surgical video not thoroughly addressed
Limited error analysis: No procedure-specific performance breakdown, no failure case analysis, no discussion of which procedures generalize well versus poorly across datasets

Experimental design gaps: Standard splits used without justification; only 50% for low-data experiments (missing full efficiency curves); some comparisons incomplete (LoViT missing M2CAI16 in Table 3)

strengths: Substantial scale and procedural diversity: 4,194 videos across 35 procedures, far exceeding existing public datasets in both size and scope
Rigorous multi-stage data curation pipeline with systematic filtering (94.75% storyboard F1, 95.64% frame F1, manual verification), demonstrating clear advantage over uncurated alternatives
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 tasks on 6 datasets with both linear probing and full fine-tuning, including data efficiency and ablation studies
Consistent strong empirical results with substantial improvements across all downstream tasks (>8pp Jaccard on phase recognition, +8.3pp mDice on segmentation)
Reproducibility commitment with detailed supplementary material and promised code/data release
weaknesses: Critical unresolved ethical concerns: patient privacy implications, uncertain licensing of YouTube sources, and inadequate consent frameworks that could severely limit reproducibility and adoption in regulated environments

Limited methodological novelty: augmented distillation is an incremental extension of DINO combining standard k-NN retrieval and temporal consistency; ablation shows only +3.2pp gain over vanilla DINO
Significant dataset composition biases not thoroughly analyzed: cholecystectomy dominates; no minimum sample analysis per procedure; train/test distribution across procedures undefined
Imperfect data curation artifacts: YOLO-based content detection at 79.29% mAP50 introduces false positives/negatives with no analysis of impact on downstream performance

Questionable annotation quality: no inter-rater reliability reporting; ChatGPT-assisted labels unvalidated; procedure classification achieving only 57.8% mAP raises concerns about annotation consistency

Incomplete baseline comparisons: Endo-FM uses private data limiting fair comparison; GenSurgery/SurgeNetXL comparison partially confounds curation benefit with data collection; missing recent video foundation model baselines
Limited failure mode analysis: no error breakdown by procedure type, no investigation of whether improvements are driven by common vs. rare procedures, no out-of-distribution generalization testing
Statistical rigor insufficient: no significance testing, confidence intervals, or multiple runs reported; some improvements modest (e.g., +4.4pp mAP on CholecT50) without error analysis
Scope limitations not clearly bounded: restricted to monocular endoscopic laparoscopic procedures; generalization to other surgical domains unestablished; 'foundation model' claims may be overstated
Dataset accessibility concerns: depends on YouTube permanence; LMDB format distribution may limit adoption; no centralized permanent hosting mentioned

strengths: Substantial dataset scale and scope: 4,194 videos (938 hours, 35 procedures) significantly exceeds prior open-access surgical datasets, addressing a documented bottleneck
Rigorous, systematic data curation pipeline with multi-stage filtering (storyboards, frame classification, object detection) and thorough documentation; >95% F1-score for key components

Comprehensive empirical evaluation across 4 downstream tasks on 6 datasets with both linear probing and full fine-tuning; strong consistent improvements (+8-9pp Jaccard in phase recognition, +8.3pp mDice in segmentation)
Well-motivated augmented distillation approach combining k-NN from same-procedure videos with temporal neighbors to learn surgical invariances; validated through ablation studies
Thorough ablations examining dataset quality impact, architecture choices (ConvNeXt vs. ViT), and pretraining objectives; demonstrates data efficiency (50% labeled data performance)
High reproducibility: detailed methods, training configurations, code/data release promised, and extensive supplementary material with curation pipeline performance metrics
Open licensing (CC BY 4.0) and public release will enable community adoption and downstream research
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: LemonFM builds incrementally on DINO (2021) by adding augmented neighbors to the augmentation pool; the +3.2pp mDice improvement over vanilla DINO is modest

Unclear contribution attribution: cannot isolate whether improvements stem from the augmented distillation method, increased dataset scale, or superior data curation; missing equivalent-scale dataset comparison
Insufficient statistical rigor: single training seed (30) for main results, no confidence intervals or significance tests, and no multiple-run variance reporting limits result reliability

Data labeling concerns: ChatGPT-v4 procedure annotation success rate not reported, only final labels manually verified, and no inter-annotator agreement metrics despite reliance on manual verification

Limited scope and generalization: evaluation restricted to minimally invasive surgery; no transfer studies to open surgery or other surgical domains; YouTube bias toward popular procedures not discussed
Missing ablation analysis: hyperparameter choices (3× distance threshold, K=20, capacity-4 pool) lack justification; no sensitivity analysis or visualization of what augmented distillation learns
Video classification task performance weak (57.8% mAP): causes of poor performance on multi-label procedure classification not analyzed; suggests potential annotation or task-design issues

Ethical/reproducibility concerns: patient privacy implications of YouTube surgical videos minimally addressed; ChatGPT-v4 API specificity limits future reproducibility; data consent status from YouTube sources unclear
No failure mode analysis: missing investigation of which procedures/tasks underperform; no visualization of learned representations or common error patterns
Statistical rigor of ablations in Table 5 questionable: single runs without error bars weaken claims about design choices

strengths: Substantial dataset contribution: LEMON (938h, 4194 videos, 35 procedures) significantly exceeds existing surgical datasets in scale and breadth, addressing genuine data scarcity in medical AI

Rigorous and reproducible data curation pipeline: multi-stage filtering achieves 100% video-level and >99.9% frame-level precision, validated by high inter-rater agreement (Cohen's Kappa 0.97) and 106 hours of expert review

Comprehensive experimental validation: evaluates on 6 independent datasets across 4 tasks with both linear probing and full fine-tuning; 5-fold cross-validation demonstrates stability (low std in Table 5); consistent improvements across all settings (+9.5pp to +10.3pp on different tasks)

Well-designed augmented distillation method: combines k-NN neighbor mining with temporal augmentations to learn invariance to patient appearance and motion variations; validated through ablations showing +3.2pp improvement over DINO
Practical efficiency: LemonFM achieves 7.8-8.9ms inference (vs. 65ms for VideoMAEv2) with two backbone options for diverse computational constraints; real-time suitability documented

Strong open science commitment: promises public dataset, code, and models under CC-BY 4.0; extensive supplementary material (9 pages) enables reproduction; provides download code and opt-out mechanism

Robust data quality metrics: comprehensive cross-validation of classifiers (storyboard F1: 94.75%, frame classification F1: 95.64%, bounding box mAP50-95: 66.18%) with detailed performance tables; procedures independently verified
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: augmented distillation is fundamentally DINO + surgical augmentations (k-NN with cosine thresholding). The 3× threshold appears empirically tuned rather than principled. Neighbor selection methodology is standard practice acknowledged in related work (SwAV, NNCLR)

Insufficient data quality and bias analysis: (1) remaining 4.36% frame classification errors could introduce subtle artifacts; (2) only 11.9% of videos independently verified; (3) procedure distribution highly imbalanced (Figure 5) with no quantitative analysis; (4) no investigation of hospital/regional/surgeon biases in YouTube sourcing; (5) procedure classification achieves only 57.8% mAP (Table 7), suggesting unexamined data ambiguity

Evaluation gaps limit generalization claims: (1) all 6 datasets focus exclusively on laparoscopic/endoscopic procedures—no evaluation on unseen modalities (open surgery, different robotic systems); (2) video classification task (novel contribution) underexplored; only brief mention of procedure confusion; (3) no systematic failure analysis identifying which scenarios/procedures cause model struggles; (4) limited ablation isolating dataset scale vs. curation quality contribution

Methodological concerns: (1) ChatGPT v4 used for annotation without validation of outputs or discussion of version drift; (2) dataset sustainability threatened by YouTube video removal over time; (3) no statistical significance testing despite improvements; (4) confidence intervals absent from main results; (5) comparison with Endo-FM confounded by 'Private data' baseline, preventing isolation of method vs. dataset contribution

Incomplete technical specifications: (1) exact k-NN retrieval mechanism (approximate vs. exact search) unspecified; (2) computational overhead of neighbor mining during training not quantified; (3) ConvNeXt vastly outperforms ViT (+10.7pp mDice, Table 6) but explanation is speculative, not empirically validated; (4) typicality weighting (Eq. 2) appears ad-hoc with limited justification

Reproducibility and sustainability concerns: (1) training requires 8 V100 GPUs for 60 epochs—significant reproduction barrier; (2) dataset links to original YouTube videos will degrade; (3) curation thresholds (90% surgical frames, 70% classifier confidence) lack principled justification; (4) no provided implementation details for neighbor selection; (5) ChatGPT version dependency makes annotation non-reproducible

Evaluation protocol inconsistencies: (1) frame-level metrics (Acc/F1) for linear probing, video-level (Acc/Jaccard) for fine-tuning makes cross-comparison harder; (2) 5-fold cross-validation stratification strategy not described; (3) early stopping criterion (10 epochs if validation loss plateaus) unjustified; (4) mixed evaluation protocols (official splits vs. 75/25 splits) across datasets

Incremental dataset methodology: While substantially larger, LEMON fundamentally uses the same YouTube sourcing as GenSurgery/SurgeNetXL. Main difference is curation rigor. Table 6 (rows 3-4) shows curation provides modest +4.5pp gain in phase recognition, raising questions about whether scale or curation drives improvements

strengths: Substantial and systematically curated dataset: LEMON (4,194 videos, 938 hours) represents a meaningful scale increase over existing public surgical datasets, with rigorous multi-stage curation achieving >99.9% precision at frame level and Cohen's Kappa 0.97 for validation
Comprehensive evaluation: Testing on 6 datasets across 4 downstream tasks with both linear probing and full fine-tuning protocols, plus 5-fold cross-validation demonstrating stable performance
Consistent empirical improvements: Systematic gains of 8-10pp on phase recognition (Jaccard), 10pp+ on semantic segmentation, and maintained advantages with 50% labeled data
Thorough ablation studies: Table 6 properly isolates contributions of dataset curation, augmented distillation, backbone architecture, and self-supervision method choices
Transparency and reproducibility: Detailed documentation of 106 person-hours of expert annotation, inter-rater agreement, computational costs, and ethical considerations
Practical efficiency: Achieves real-time inference (7.8-8.9ms) suitable for clinical deployment while maintaining competitive accuracy
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: Augmented distillation (Eq. 1) is essentially DINO with procedurally-informed neighbors—intuitive but incremental. The 3× distance threshold appears heuristic rather than theoretically grounded

Unclear performance attribution: Table 6 shows LEMON without augmented distillation achieves 71.7/61.4 F1, while with augmentation it reaches 76.4/66.9 (+5.5pp F1), suggesting the dataset drives most improvements; relative contributions are poorly decomposed

Dataset bias and scope limitations: No quantitative analysis of highly skewed procedure distribution (Figure 5), institutional/geographic biases from YouTube sourcing, or generalization beyond laparoscopy. Dependence on ChatGPT-v4 for annotation raises reproducibility concerns

Weak video classification results undermine dataset quality claims: Proposed procedure type classification achieves only 57.8% mAP; brief acknowledgment of anatomical confusion without deeper error analysis or solutions suggests model struggles with core dataset utility
Incomplete baseline comparisons: Table 3 specialist models (TeCNO, Trans-SVNet, LoViT) use results from prior work (†) rather than retraining with unified protocols, limiting claims of superiority

Data validation gaps: Inter-rater agreement on only ~500 videos with 2 raters; no analysis of disagreement categories, resolution strategies, or annotation difficulty; high Kappa doesn't guarantee robustness to systematic bias

Missing theoretical justification: The choice of k-NN from same procedure type + temporal neighbors lacks explicit motivation beyond intuition; why this particular augmentation strategy over alternatives?

Limited failure analysis: No per-procedure performance breakdown, no investigation of cross-dataset domain gaps, no empirical validation of ConvNeXt's claimed ability to preserve fine-grained surgical details versus ViT

strengths: Largest public surgical dataset to date (4,194 videos, 938 hours) with rigorous multi-stage curation pipeline achieving >99.9% precision at frame level and 100% at video level

Comprehensive experimental validation across 6 datasets and 4 downstream tasks with consistent, substantial improvements (+9.5pp Jaccard phase recognition, +10.3pp mDice segmentation, +5.3-10.2pp tool detection)
Thorough ablation studies systematically validating dataset scale, curation importance, and design choices with clear justification for architectural decisions
Robust evaluation with 5-fold cross-validation and low standard deviations; strong performance in low-data regime (50% data outperforms other methods on 100% data)
Surgical-specific innovations well-motivated: augmented distillation designed for patient appearance invariance and motion invariance with 3× threshold validated by ablation
Practical efficiency with real-time inference (≤7.8ms per frame) while maintaining state-of-the-art performance; substantially faster than VideoMAEv2 (15.6pp mDice gain)
Exemplary transparency: rigorous ethical considerations, detailed annotation procedures (Cohen's Kappa 0.97), detailed implementation details in supplementary material, and public release commitment
Clear presentation with informative figures (especially curation pipeline) and comprehensive tables; extensive supplementary material with hyperparameters and training configurations
weaknesses: Dataset source bias: Exclusive YouTube collection may systematically exclude challenging real-world cases and rare complications; geographic/institutional diversity not analyzed; educational nature may not reflect OR practice variability

Limited core technical novelty: Augmented distillation extends DINO incrementally; improvements over vanilla DINO are modest (+3.2pp mDice); neighbor selection threshold (3×) justified by ablation but lacks deeper theoretical motivation
New procedure classification task achieves only 57.8% mAP with acknowledged confusions between anatomically similar procedures; limited root cause analysis or systematic failure mode investigation

Temporal surgical workflow patterns may be underutilized: Frame-based architecture justified for efficiency but may miss sequential phase progressions and temporal surgical patterns captured by video-based models
Incomplete generalization analysis: No per-procedure performance breakdown; uncertain how model generalizes to rare procedures; class imbalance across procedures (Figure 5) impact unexplored

Baseline comparison complexity: Endo-FM uses private data (unfair comparison); SurgeNetXL comparison confounds data scale with method improvements; no statistical significance testing despite apparent significance from low standard deviations
Scope limitation to minimally invasive laparoscopic surgery: No evaluation on open surgery or alternative modalities; foundation model claim somewhat overstated given procedural scope constraints

Annotation coverage lean for dataset scale: 106 hours annotation by 2 PhD researchers for 85M frames (0.00125 annotations/frame); inter-rater reliability only on 500-video subset; annotation guidelines not detailed

No clinical validation linking CV improvements to surgical outcomes or surgeon acceptance; no domain expert assessment of dataset quality or model predictions; false positive/negative clinical implications not discussed

Incomplete artifact analysis: Residual non-surgical content not systematically characterized; video quality variation across procedure types and sources not analyzed; impact of obliterated regions on model training unexplored
